title: Arrays
theory:
## Arrays in Go

Arrays in Go are fixed-size sequences of elements of the same type.

### Array Declaration

```go
var arr [5]int              // array of 5 ints, zero-initialized
arr := [5]int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5} // array with initial values
```

### Key Properties of Arrays

1. **Fixed size**: The size is part of the type - [5]int is different from [6]int
2. **Value type**: Arrays are copied when assigned or passed to functions
3. **Zero-initialized**: Elements get their zero value if not specified

```go
arr := [4]int{1, 2} // arr = [1, 2, 0, 0]
```

### Array Iteration with Range

```go
for index, value := range arr {
    fmt.Println(index, value)
}
```

Use `_` to ignore the index or value:
```go
for _, v := range arr {
    fmt.Println(v)
}
```

### Multi-dimensional Arrays

```go
matrix := [2][3]int{
    {1, 2, 3},
    {4, 5, 6},
}
```

exercises.title: Create Array
exercises.description: Create an array of 5 ints with values 1,2,3,4,5. Print all elements.

exercises.title: Array Iteration
exercises.description: Create array nums := [3]int{10, 20, 30}. Use range to print each element.
hints: Use for i, v := range nums { fmt.Println(v) }

exercises.title: Array Length
exercises.description: Create arr := [4]int{1, 2, 3, 4}. Print the length using len(arr).
hints: Use len(arr) to get array length

exercises.title: Partial Array Initialization
exercises.description: Create an array of 5 ints where only the first two are initialized to 10 and 20. Print the array.

exercises.title: 2D Array
exercises.description: Create a 2x2 matrix with values {{1, 2}, {3, 4}}. Print each element on separate lines.
hints: Use nested range or direct indexing

exercises.title: Array Sum
exercises.description: Create arr := [5]int{10, 20, 30, 40, 50}. Compute the sum of all elements and print it.
hints: Use range to iterate and accumulate: sum += v

exercises.title: Array Element Access
exercises.description: Create arr := [3]int{100, 200, 300}. Print the first element (index 0) and last element (index 2).
hints: arr[0] is first, arr[2] is last
